notes.6: Question 6 was answered correctly by 35% who chose option B. 12% chose option A, 6% chose option C and 47% chose option D. Option D would increase the supply and cause the supply curve to shift, any change in demand would be represented as a movement along the existing demand curve. Options A and C would shift the demand curve in the opposite direction to that shown on the diagram.
notes.18: Question 18 was answered correctly by 34% who chose option D. 18% chose option A, 17% chose option B and 31% chose option C. When the tax is imposed the new equilibrium quantity would be Q and the new price T. The government would receive TUZY. Compared with the original price (V) the consumer would pay part of the tax (TUWV – option C) but the producer also has to pay part of the tax. Options A and B involve the original quantity (E) which becomes irrelevant. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0455 Economics November 2015
notes.25: Question 25 was answered correctly by 24% of the candidates who chose option B. 67% chose option A, and 9% chose option D. No candidate chose option C.
